I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything fancy. On my 7.5 mu, I’ll still keep cotton as the main crop. Cotton gives me cash if the year is decent, and I know how to manage it. But I won’t put all land into cotton. I’ll keep 2.5 mu in wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That way, even if cotton price is no good or weather turns bad, I still have grain from the wheat-maize land. I have only two people at home, so I must keep the work something we can manage ourselves, and I can’t spend too much cash all at once.

For cotton, I’ll plant about the usual time in April, use seed I can get locally, put base fertilizer first, then add a bit more later if the plants look weak. Cotton needs watching for worms and weeds, so I’ll spray only when I see a real problem. Since I have well water, I’ll irrigate, but not too many times because pumping costs money. For wheat, I’ll do it the old way, sow in October, put some fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once in spring if the seedlings look yellow. Wheat cannot be starved too much or yield drops badly. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll rush to plant maize on that same land. That turnaround is always tight, so I’ll do simple tillage, not heavy work. Maize grows fast in summer, so I’ll give it one main fertilizer dose and maybe one watering if rain is short. This way, I keep costs under control, keep some grain coming, and still leave most land in cotton for cash.
